say: You think Earth is big? Watch it disappear.
Jupiter. Eleven Earths fit side by side across it.
The Sun. A hundred and nine Earths wide, and over ninety nine percent of the Solar System's mass.
Rigel. A blue supergiant, seventy nine times wider than the Sun.
Betelgeuse. Put it where the Sun is, and it swallows Mars.
Stephenson two eighteen. Possibly the biggest star known. It would reach past Jupiter.
Our entire Solar System, out to Neptune. Light needs eight hours to cross it.
The Orion Nebula. Twenty four light years of glowing gas, where stars are born.
The Milky Way. A hundred thousand light years, and hundreds of billions of stars. We're right here.
Laniakea, our supercluster. A hundred thousand galaxies, five hundred twenty million light years wide.
And number one. The observable universe. Ninety three billion light years. And it might be a tiny piece of everything.
Which one broke your brain? Tell me in the comments.
